author: reek
body: Declarative form validation, with four real consumers -- WorkflowHtml, DiffusionApp, TrackerApp and the foreword's own SettingsPanel -- and no test anywhere. A validator is the worst thing in the tree to leave unmeasured: every caller believes its verdict, and a wrong "valid" is accepted in silence by all of them.

author: reek
body: Each rule is asked for a value it must ACCEPT and a value it must REJECT. A rule tested only on the accepting side cannot tell a working check from one that always answers VrOk, and a rule tested only on the rejecting side cannot tell one from a check that always answers VrError.

author: reek
body: `Validation` used to name those numbers itself, which made it the third place in the tree spelling out what a letter is, and the three drifted apart the moment one moved. It asks `cce-is-letter-any` now. The rule for this chapter is therefore the inverse of what it used to be: a RANGE appearing here at all is the thing to be suspicious of.

author: reek
body: A digit is Tier 0 by construction, so a multi-byte character is not one however letter-like it looks.

author: reek
body: Two fields, the second of which must fail, so a form that reported valid would be reporting it over a field it had actually rejected.

author: reek
body: An error is withheld until the field has been touched. That is the chapter's stated behaviour and it means the message is empty for a field that genuinely failed, which is worth pinning in both states.
